newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish MPs want to restrict child labour.
newsitem.headline: Polish MPs want to restrict child labour.

text.p: A Polish parliamentary conference called on Monday for tighter restrictions on child labour, saying minors were being increasingly exploited by employers.
Conference participants noted that Polish laws prohibiting the employment of those under 15, restricting the kinds of work they may do and banning overtime were openly ignored.

"Adherence to these rules is very poor and violation of basic work-safety regulations poses a direct threat to the health of our young people," State Labour Inspector Anna Hintz told private Radio Zet.
The conference, organised by the Parliamentary Children's Affairs Group, heard reports that minors work on night shifts in private bakeries and often go unpaid for months at a time.
The worst off are farm children who are often forced by their parents to perform back-breaking labour amid dangerous agricultural machines.
"A list of jobs which minors may not perform should be the first step towards preventing their exploitation," said the chairwoman of the parliamentary group, Katarzyna Piekarska.
"It is reprehensible if children are forced to work at great heights, operate unprotected machinery and lug loads nearly equalling their own body weight."
